subject: Climate & Environment
title: Ocean Renewable Energy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Ocean Renewable Energy usable.

hook.text: The ocean holds vast untapped energy — in waves, tides, currents, and temperature differences.

buildup.text: Tidal energy is highly predictable — unlike wind or solar, you know exactly when tides come in.

discovery.text: Wave energy devices convert the up-and-down motion of swells into electricity.

twist.text: Ocean thermal energy uses the temperature gap between surface and deep water to generate power.

climax.text: These technologies are still early-stage but could power coastal communities sustainably.

punchline.text: The ocean never stops moving. That motion is energy waiting to be captured.

quiz.question: What advantage does tidal energy have over wind or solar?

details.summary: The ocean offers multiple renewable energy sources including offshore wind, tidal power, wave energy, and ocean thermal energy conversion. Offshore wind is already a major and rapidly growing electricity source, while tidal and wave technologies are still maturing toward commercial viability.
details.whyItMatters: Ocean energy could provide a significant share of global electricity demand. Offshore wind alone is projected to become one of the largest power sources this century.
takeaways: Offshore wind is the most mature ocean energy technology
Tidal energy harnesses predictable tidal flows for power
Wave and thermal energy technologies are still developing

faq.question: How much energy could the ocean provide?
faq.answer: Theoretical ocean energy potential exceeds current global electricity demand many times over. Offshore wind alone could technically supply all of it. Practical deployment depends on costs, grid integration, and environmental considerations.

faq.question: What are the environmental concerns of ocean energy?
faq.answer: Offshore wind turbines can affect seabirds and marine mammals. Tidal barrages alter sediment flow and habitat. Subsea cables and foundations create electromagnetic fields. However, impacts are generally far smaller than those of fossil fuel extraction.
